translations.answer: SafeFall uses a GRU to predict imminent failure of a nominal policy and hands control to a protective policy. The paper reduces contact force and joint torque in simulation and reports a limited hardware impulse experiment. The predictor must be retrained when the nominal policy changes, the environments are flat or nearly flat, and no public implementation was found, so this is not a cross-platform, all-terrain safety guarantee.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: Failure trajectories have been resampled and the predictor retrained for the current nominal policy.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Protective-policy trigger thresholds, contact surfaces, and robot hardware have passed staged safety validation.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: GRU failure predictor and protective mitigation policy
translations.applicability.environments.0: Instability, collision, and fall mitigation on flat or approximately flat terrain
translations.applicability.robots.0: The humanoid hardware used in the paper; platform changes require renewed validation
translations.applicability.simulators.0: Large-scale simulated failure trajectories and a limited physical-robot impulse experiment
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper reports large simulation metrics and a limited hardware impact result. The settings are nearly flat, the predictor depends on the nominal policy, and no official public code was found during review.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines failure prediction, policy handoff, and protective objectives, then reports simulated impact reduction and bounded hardware validation.
translations.evidence.0.title: SafeFall: Learning Protective Control for Humanoid Robots
translations.terms.1: Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU, 门控循环单元)
translations.title: Is SafeFall a general safety layer that needs no controller-specific retraining and guarantees damage-free falls on arbitrary terrain?
